subject: Azure Private Plan - termination triggers & risk allocation
messages:
From: Elisa Turner <elisa.turner@harrishealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@harrishealth.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Azure Private Plan - termination triggers and holdback question

Irene / Jonas,

Thanks for the updated private plan term sheet. Our procurement team reviewed and surfaced two items that need clearer language before we can take this to legal:

1) Termination triggers: the current draft allows immediate termination for certain breaches but doesn’t define a cure period. We need a 60-90 day cure for non-SLA breaches; for material breaches that affect PHI handling we may need earlier escalation language.

2) Financial protection / holdback: given the multi-year commitment and downstream risk to our billing workflow we are requesting a 6% holdback on the first quarter's invoice against undisclosed performance defects, or alternatively an SLA credit multiplier that accrues until remediation.

I attached a marked copy (HHS_Redlines_05025.docx) with suggested language. Can Redwood confirm whether a 60-day cure + pro-rata SLA credit (capped at 25% of quarterly fees) is acceptable?

Also copying Michael Lopez from our legal team who will add formal redlines. We are hoping to finalize commercial terms this week so we can get to signing early June.

Best,
Elisa Turner
Senior Procurement Manager
Harris Health Systems

Attachment: HHS_Redlines_05025.docx (docx)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elisa Turner <elisa.turner@harrishealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure Private Plan - termination triggers and holdback question

Hi Elisa —

Thanks for the detailed note and the marked copy. We appreciate the clarity. Quick responses to your two bullets below, with a proposed compromise attached (Redwood_Harris_TermSheet_v2.pdf):

- Cure period: Redwood agrees to a 60-day cure for non-SLA material breaches (we can drop to 30 days if the breach relates to security or PHI handling). For SLA failures, we will follow the credit process outlined in Section 4.2 (immediate rectification steps + pro-rata credits).

- Holdback: We prefer SLA credits vs. a cash holdback to keep invoicing simple. Proposal: pro-rata SLA credits accrued daily for the impacted pool, capped at 30% of the quarterly invoice for recurring services, with a contractual right for you to request a remediation plan and temporary stop-gap mitigation. If you require a cash holdback as an alternative, we can discuss a 3% retention to be released after 90 days post-activation.

Marissa is looped in on the specific termination language. If acceptable, we can consolidate into a single redline and move to DocuSign.

Next steps: 1) Jonas/Elisa, confirm whether SLA-credit cap or 3% retention is preferred. 2) If SLA credits, Marissa will send the counter-language today.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Harris_TermSheet_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: Michael Lopez <m.lopez@harrishealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Elisa Turner <elisa.turner@harrishealth.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 08:27:00 -05:00
Subject: HHS redlines - termination and remedies

Irene / Elisa / Jonas,

Attached are our formal redlines. Key requests from legal:

- A 90-day cure period for non-security material breaches; 30-day cure for security/PHI incidents with immediate interim mitigation obligations.
- Termination for convenience: Harris requests a 60-day notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
- Remedies: we propose SLA credits plus an upset cap on Redwood's liability tied to fees (12 months of fees) and an express carveout for wilful misconduct.
- Audit rights: limited to annually and scoped to access logs and controls for a 30-day lookback; Redwood must provide evidence of remediation activities for any audit finding.

We redlined termination language to make the cure period explicit and added a short clause for escrowed source (we understand Redwood will not agree to escrow, but wanted to flag).

Please see HHS_Redlines_05025.docx (already shared). Happy to jump on a call if helpful.

— Michael Lopez
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Harris Health Systems

Attachment: HHS_Redlines_05025.docx (docx)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Lopez <m.lopez@harrishealth.com>, Elisa Turner <elisa.turner@harrishealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood counter - termination, cure period and credit cap

Michael / Elisa —

Thanks for the redlines. Redwood's counter-proposal on the key commercial/legal points is below; I’ve attached a tracked redline (Redwood_Counter_termination_SN.docx) with exact language.

1) Cure period: Redwood can accept a 60-day cure for general material breaches and 30 days for security/PHI-related incidents. We will include explicit interim mitigation obligations for security incidents (notification, containment plan, remediation milestones) to address Harris's concerns.

2) Termination for convenience: Redwood agrees to a 60-day notice, but requests that any prepaid fees for managed services be handled via pro-rata credits rather than immediate cash refunds (we will issue credits against future bills within the same fiscal year). This protects both sides operationally.

3) SLA credits vs. holdback: Redwood stands by the SLA-credit model. Proposed mechanics: daily accrual based on impacted capacity, credited monthly, cap at 25% of quarterly recurring fees (we can go to 30% one-time if Harris insists). We will include a remediation playbook by activation to reduce recurrence risk.

4) Liability cap: Redwood proposes a liability cap of 12 months of fees for direct damages, excluding gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

5) Audit rights: Redwood will allow one limited, vendor-led audit per year; we will provide access logs and an attestation of remediation actions. Full on-site audits to be limited to incidents and by mutual agreement.

If this framework is acceptable, I recommend a short commercial call (30 minutes) to finalize a single redline. Jonas — can you share availability tomorrow morning?

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Team —

Appreciate the quick turns this week. Summary and proposed next steps so we can close commercial terms:

Summary of agreement in principle
- Cure period: 60 days for general material breaches; 30 days for security/PHI incidents with immediate mitigation obligations.
- Termination for convenience: 60-day notice. Prepaid fees handled via pro-rata credits (Harris to confirm if cash refund is must-have).
- SLA remediation: daily accrual, monthly crediting, cap at 25% of quarterly recurring fees (Redwood can move to 30% one-time if Harris requires).
- Liability: cap at 12 months of fees; carveout for wilful misconduct.
- Audit: one vendor-led annual audit; incident-triggered audits by mutual agreement.

Action items
1) Elisa/Michael — confirm cash refund vs. credits preference by EOD Monday (2027-05-31).
2) Marissa — finalize tracked redline and upload to DocuSign powerform (target: Tue 2027-06-01).
3) Jonas — prepare mutual action plan and order form reflecting the agreed caps/credits; share HubSpot link.
